atomicity.description: Critical business flows (holds, checkout, scanning) MUST use atomic Ash actions with proper locking (LOCKS-1).
requirements: require_atomic? true for all critical actions.
No direct side effects (emails, HTTP calls) inside atomic change blocks.
Conflicting updates MUST surface as Ash.Error.Invalid with LOCKS-1 error codes.
All business logic MUST be accessed via Ash.Domain actions (Ash 3.x naming).
Direct calls that bypass Domains MUST NOT be used as the public boundary.
All hot-path operations listed in hot_path_latency_budgets MUST be measurable via telemetry histograms.
Telemetry metadata MUST include org_id (tenant), operation_id, correlation_id, and result_class (ok|error|rejected).
Custom operation spans MAY be emitted via Ash.Tracer.telemetry_span/3 from hot-path hooks (no side effects).
Custom event namespace MUST be [:ticketing, :op, ...]; do NOT use [:v42, ...] as project-level namespace.

ash_concurrency_limits.principle: All API-exposed Ash actions MUST be assigned to a concurrency group with a per-node max concurrency cap.

budget_ownership.change_control: PSC-1 update + observability policy regeneration + sign-off (product+infra)

failure_isolation.rule: Saturation in non-primary pools MUST NOT starve primary pool connections.

notes: Latency profiles are distinct from PSC-1 load_profiles. load_profiles model system-wide traffic shape (e.g., HOT_SALE, WEBHOOK_STORM). latency_profile_registry models per-queue job classes for async workers.
Other contracts that reference a PSC-1 latency profile MUST use an id from this registry. Unknown profile ids are forbidden.
The HEAVY profile quota is an SLO-safety default. Implementations MAY tighten per domain; they MUST NOT loosen without GOV-0 break-glass approval and documented risk acceptance.

profiles.description: Default async-job latency profile for user-facing or time-sensitive work. Expected to complete quickly and MUST be prioritized over HEAVY work during contention.
Async-job latency profile for compute-heavy or IO-heavy work (bulk exports, large reconciliations, backfills). HEAVY work MUST be quota-limited and MUST NOT starve STANDARD work.

load_profiles.description: Typical day-to-day traffic with small events and moderate webhooks.
High concurrency on queue, seatmap, holds, and checkout during major on-sales.
High traffic on scan decisions during event entry windows.
Inbound provider webhook spike (refunds, chargebacks, payouts).

rules: All cache keys used on hot paths MUST be tenant-scoped by org_id (directly or via tenant-derived namespace).
Admission control and rate limiting MUST NOT allow one tenant/org_id to consume capacity allocated to another tenant/org_id (no global buckets) unless explicitly permitted by contract.
Queue tickets and buyer sessions MUST be cryptographically bound to org_id and MUST be rejected if org_id does not match current tenant context.

query_shape_bans.text: Offset pagination (OFFSET/LIMIT) MUST NOT be used for public API reads past page 10; use keyset pagination.
Sorting on non-indexed, unbounded fields for public endpoints is forbidden during HOT_SALE.

references.ref: Google SRE Workbook - Alerting on SLOs

rules.text: PSC-1 and PSC-1-GATE MUST be JSON-only normative artifacts; repacks are forbidden; metadata must match filenames and manifest pins.

rules.rationale: If it isn't budgeted, it won't be protected, and it will fail under load.
rules.text: Every critical operation listed in API-0 MUST map to an explicit hot-path latency budget (p50/p95/p99) or an explicit 'out of scope' justification.

rules.rationale: Performance regressions must be caught by CI, not human intuition.
rules.text: Latency budgets MUST be enforced via automated load tests; manual-only verification is forbidden.

rules.rationale: Backpressure keeps the platform alive during spikes.
rules.text: Admission control MUST define overload signals, load-shed responses, and retry guidance. These apply globally across all load profiles unless a profile-specific override is declared in the profile definition.

rules.rationale: High-cardinality metrics will melt the TSDB during incidents.
rules.text: Performance metrics MUST NOT label by org_id (tenant key), actor_id, request_id, or any unbounded identifiers. Use aggregated dimensions only (e.g., org_tier, region).

rules.rationale: DB pool exhaustion is a common throughput limiter and source of cascading failures.
rules.text: DB connection leasing MUST comply with PSC-1 connection_leasing invariants (checkout p95/p99 and pool timeout).

rules.rationale: Ensures data integrity under concurrent load.
rules.text: All critical business actions listed in hot_path_latency_budgets MUST be implemented as Ash atomic actions with require_atomic? true and LOCKS-1-compliant locking.

rules.rationale: Without telemetry, budgets cannot be validated or alerted on.
rules.text: Hot-path Ash actions MUST emit telemetry events ticketing.ash.action.start/stop OR leverage standard Ash telemetry [:ash, (domain_short_name), :action, :start|:stop] with org_id metadata.

rules.rationale: Load profile IDs and operational flags use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE by convention for ENV-like operational constants.
rules.text: Enum identifiers for load profiles and operational flags MAY use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (e.g., HOT_SALE, WEBHOOK_SHED_MODE). All other identifiers MUST use snake_case.

Aggregate analytics surfaces SHALL enforce an anonymization threshold of min_population_size=5 with complementary suppression, and SHALL apply anti-differencing controls (query normalization, minimum time windows, caching, and rate limiting) as specified in /privacy_analytics_controls.

PSC-1 MUST define a latency_profile_registry that is the sole authority for latency profile ids referenced by worker-queue and backpressure contracts. The registry MUST include at minimum: STANDARD and HEAVY, and MUST declare default_profile_id = STANDARD.

Any contract referencing a PSC-1 latency profile (e.g., OBQC-1 queue policies) MUST use a profile id defined in PSC-1.latency_profile_registry.profiles[].id. Unknown profile ids MUST be rejected at contract-review time and by test gates where applicable.

HEAVY latency profile work MUST be quota-limited per domain using PSC-1.latency_profile_registry.heavy_quota_fraction_default (or stricter) to prevent starvation of STANDARD work. Any relaxation MUST require GOV-0 break-glass approval and an audit trail.
FeeSchedule lookup and platform fee computation MUST be O(1) per checkout intent: implementations MUST NOT execute per-line-item DB queries or N+1 fetches to compute platform fees.

Platform fee computation MUST be system-only and deterministic: any client-supplied fee fields (e.g., fee_lines, fee_total_minor) MUST be rejected or ignored; the server MUST recompute via PAY-3 fee engine.

rules.rationale: Pure 503 load-shedding creates retry storms and guarantees collapse under flash-sale demand.
rules.text: During HOT_SALE profile, all hot-path endpoints MUST enforce a virtual waiting room / queue-token gate OR an equivalent deterministic admission control mechanism; naive 503-only load shedding is forbidden.

rules.rationale: Long-running statements and lock waits are fatal under flash-sale concurrency; timeouts enforce fail-fast backpressure.
rules.text: Public-facing DB pools MUST enforce statement_timeout <= 3000ms and lock_timeout <= 500ms. Exceptions MUST be isolated to non-primary pools.

rules.rationale: Deep OFFSET paging is a common DoS vector and causes non-linear DB cost growth.
rules.text: Public reads MUST use keyset pagination. Offset pagination is forbidden beyond page 10.

rules.rationale: Bulkheading prevents non-critical queries from starving the transactional hot path.
rules.text: Reporting/analytics workloads MUST be isolated to a read_replica pool and MUST NOT consume primary transactional connections.

rules.rationale: Unbounded task spawning can collapse the BEAM scheduler even if Postgres remains healthy.
rules.text: API-exposed Ash actions MUST be protected by per-node concurrency caps (bulkheads). Concurrency groups MUST be explicit and stable.

summary: Defines latency budgets, load profiles, connection-leasing invariants, and Ash 3.x performance patterns with machine-enforced evidence requirements (load tests, atomicity audits, telemetry capture).
